mutation.m1.retirement.direct_rollover_p: Mutation fixture (whether money went back into a retirement account, for a direct rollover), inputs of stage10.plan.direct_rollover with its defaults stated (a plan distribution of $20,000, code G); expected value predicted by hand from the archived f1099r before running the evaluator: code G is a direct rollover to another plan or IRA (f1099r Box 7, code G), so the money went into another retirement account (person.retirement.put_back true), without the rollover question being asked.
mutation.m1.retirement.partial_rollover_: Mutation fixture (whether money went back into a retirement account, for a rollover the filer reports), inputs of stage10.ira.partial_rollover with its defaults stated (an IRA distribution of $10,000, not a direct rollover, of which the filer says $6,000 was rolled over); expected value predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi before running the evaluator: the filer answered Yes to 'Did any of this money go into a retirement account again (a rollover or a conversion), even if it was paid to you first?', so some of the money went into another retirement account (person.retirement.put_back true; i1040gi p. 26, Lines 4a and 4b, Exception 1, rollovers).
mutation.m1.retirement.plan_death_code4: Mutation fixture (a payment from a plan to a beneficiary), inputs of stage10.smw.survivor_of_retiree with its defaults stated (a plan annuity paid to the survivor of a retiree, code 4); expected value predicted by hand from the archived f1099r before running the evaluator: code 4 is a death distribution paid to a beneficiary (f1099r Box 7, code 4), and the account is a plan, not an IRA, so the plan-to-beneficiary questions apply (person.retirement.plan_death true).
mutation.m1.retirement.roth_ira_code4: Mutation fixture (a death distribution from a Roth IRA is not a plan payment to a beneficiary), inputs of stage10.ira.roth_qualified with its defaults stated and the distribution code changed to 4 (death), the filer answering No to 'Did you get this money some other way?' (a beneficiary); expected value predicted by hand from the archived f1099r and i1040gi before running the evaluator: the account is a Roth IRA, so the questions for a plan's payments to a beneficiary (the death benefit exclusion and the plan-only items) do not apply (person.retirement.plan_death false); the distribution is refused as a Roth IRA distribution other than code Q (i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2).
mutation.m1.retirement.annuity_rollover_: Mutation fixture (the Simplified Method Worksheet is shown for a plan annuity with cost left, even with a rollover), inputs of stage10.refuse.annuity_rollover with its defaults stated (a plan annuity of $12,000 with after-tax cost of $31,000, code G); expected value predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi before running the evaluator: the payments are from a plan, the Simplified Method applies and cost is left to recover (i1040gi p. 28, Simplified Method Worksheet), so the worksheet is completed (person.retirement.smw_shown true); the rollover of an annuity figured by the Simplified Method is then refused.
mutation.m1.retirement.code7_under59: Mutation fixture (code 7 for a person under 59 1/2), inputs of stage10.ira.fully_taxable with its defaults stated, the distribution code 7, Yes to 'Were you under age 59½ when you received any of this money?' and No to 'Is it from a section 457 plan ...?'; expected values predicted by hand from the archived f1099r and i5329 before running the evaluator: code 7 is a normal distribution, for a person 59 1/2 or older (f1099r Box 7, code 7); for a person under 59 1/2 it fits only a section 457 plan distribution not from a rollover, so the code does not fit (person.retirement.code7_wrong true) and the Form 1099-R is refused as needing Form 5329 rules this tool does not apply (person.retirement.screen_refused true).
mutation.m1.retirement.roth_code7_under5: Mutation fixture (two refusals of one Form 1099-R: the first in order is told), inputs of stage10.refuse.roth_not_q with its defaults stated (a Roth IRA distribution), the distribution code 7, Yes to 'Were you under age 59½ when you received any of this money?' and No to the section 457 question; expected values predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi before running the evaluator: a Roth IRA distribution other than a qualified distribution (code Q) needs Form 8606 (i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2), refused, and that refusal, the first of line 4a's, is the one line 4a carries (f1040.line4a, gate bad_code); the code 7 for a person under 59 1/2 also does not fit (person.retirement.screen_refused true), a later refusal.
mutation.m1.retirement.ira_box5: Mutation fixture (an amount in box 5 of an IRA distribution's Form 1099-R does not make it partly nontaxable), inputs of stage10.ira.fully_taxable with its defaults stated (a traditional IRA distribution of $10,000, code 7) and $500 entered in box 5; expected values predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi before running the evaluator: box 5 is for after-tax employee contributions and premiums under plans and annuities (i1099r, Box 5), not for IRAs, whose nontaxable part comes from Form 8606; with no rollover, no Roth account and no basis the IRA distribution is fully taxable, so line 4a is left blank (person.retirement.amount_a $0) and the whole $10,000 goes on line 4b (i1040gi p. 26, Lines 4a and 4b).
